title: No "known good" password available for this user
plain_english: FreeRADIUS found the user but has no password (in a usable format) to check the login against — so authentication can never succeed no matter what the user types. The problem is on the server/backend side, not the client.

causes.cause: No authorize module actually supplied a password: the users file entry didn't match, the SQL query returned no rows, or the LDAP attribute wasn't fetched.
causes.next_check: In the radiusd -X output, follow the authorize section and see which module (files/sql/ldap) matched — and whether it added a *-Password attribute.

causes.cause: The password exists but in a format the chosen auth method can't use — e.g. MSCHAPv2 against an SSHA-hashed LDAP password.
causes.next_check: Check which Auth-Type was selected in the debug and whether the stored password format is compatible (PAP works with most hashes; MSCHAP needs NT hash or cleartext).

causes.cause: A typo in the users file or a schema/column mismatch in SQL means the lookup silently misses.
causes.next_check: Run the exact SQL/LDAP query from the debug output by hand and confirm it returns the password attribute.
